newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Retail stocks rally on interest rate relief.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Retail stocks rally on interest rate relief.

text.p: Shares in leading British retailers jumped on Thursday as the Bank of England's quarter-point interest rate rise was not as harsh as some had feared.
Positive trading news from the sector also contributed to the rally.
At the close, blue chip retail group Marks & Spencer Plc stood up 20 pence at 554p, after earlier scoring a record 560p, and there were strong gains through the rest of the sector.

After months of underperformance by retail stocks amid fears that rising interest rates would kill off the nascent recovery in consumer confidence, dealers said some investors were looking for a cue to buy back into top stores.
A rate rise by the Bank of England was hardly good news but the increase that took base lending rates to 6.75 percent was not as bad as the much stricter monetary medicine some had feared.
"The UK consumer is doing very well and it will take a lot more than this (rate rise) to stop him," said Ciaran Barr, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

The sector was also boosted by an upbeat trading statement from Storehouse Plc, owner of the Bhs, Mothercare and Childrens' World chains. It said same-store sales grew 14.5 percent in the first quarter.
The news came after a buoyant statement on Wednesday from electrical retailer Dixons Group Plc, which reported a 17 percent rise in sales excluding new store openings.
Dixons gained 17-1/2p to 554, after earlier reaching a year's high of 566p amid positive press and analyst comment on the results.
Good news for retailers also came this week from supermarket operator J Sainsbury Plc, which said same-store sales expanded by a greater-than-expected 4.2 percent.
Sainsbury shares were up 20p at 419 1/2, after earlier rising as high as 426p -- their highest in some 18 months.

Dealers said the spate of good trading news, coupled with interest rate relief, helped offset the poor sentiment which has dogged the sector since about last October when fears of rising rates started gaining ground.
"There's a lot of relief around in the retail sector," said one head of equity trading, "they were given a real hammering and now everyone is just very happy."
Analysts said retail shares had also gained favour in recent sessions since they were more insulated from the sterling strength that has cast a shadow over exporters and some international companies.
Being domestically-oriented, retailers have not fallen prey to the earnings downgrades that have weighed on the likes of British Steel Plc and Imperial Chemical Industries Plc in recent weeks.
"The market is responding to safety and value," one retail analyst said.

With shares prices squeezed higher by a shortage of stock among market makers, whose books have been cleaned out by recent demand, Kingfisher Plc closed up 11 at 703-1/2 after at one stage surging as much as 45-1/2p.
Among other leading retailers, catalogue retailer Argos Plc was up 26 1/2p at 592 and drugstore chain Boots Co Plc gained 9-1/2p to 791-1/2
Yet retail sector leaders had lost the bulk of their gains towards the London market's close and there were lingering doubts about the pace of growth in consumer spending through 1998.

Much of the recent consumer recovery could reflect the one-off impact of "windfall" gains from the crop of demutualising building societies works, which has put more than 30 billion stg into consumers' pockets.
Some also said there remained a risk of further rate rises to come later in the year.
"The economy is too warm and needs a little cooling," said Roger Monson, London strategist at Japanese-based brokerage Daiwa. "The thinking will turn to when we get the next increase."
